quote: The only reason I'm talking to you right now is because we installed the satellite dish.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers his motivating trigger (new satellite install prompted his current utility awareness) unprompted and at length — a highly engaged, self-qualifying lead moment.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back explicitly ("so the satellite got you thinking about power independence") to anchor the appointment conversation in the customer's own words rather than letting it pass as a background detail.

quote: I'm leaning towards the generator backup so that I don't have to rely on Dominion Energy at all ever again.
stewart_read: This is a customer independently expressing strong purchase intent and specificity (generator backup, batteries, inverter) well beyond typical solar interest — a highly qualified, self-directed lead.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep is simply staying in listening mode appropriately since the customer is doing the selling himself.
coaching_implication: Even when a customer self-sells, the rep should mark and repeat back the specificity ("total independence from Dominion") so it surfaces clearly in the handoff to the closer rather than getting buried among later details.

quote: You said that you're with Dominion. Do you know how much you're paying Dominion on average?
stewart_read: Rep captures the bill figure cleanly, but per bill_anchoring's failure_pattern ('ask + acknowledge + move on'), the number is never flipped into emotional alignment-against-the-utility — especially notable here since the customer already stated he wants zero reliance on Dominion, handing the rep a ready-made flip.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to tie the captured bill number directly to the customer's stated goal in the moment: "so that $250-450 a month to Dominion is exactly what we're aiming to eliminate" — the flip was sitting right there and went unused.

quote: Well, yeah, what I'll do, I'll send you a text here. We're looking for the exact same thing. You could just send a photo of that to me here.
stewart_read: Customer is mobile and away from home (in his truck); rep pivots immediately to the text-photo path without friction, matching the schema's shopping_customer_protocol guidance for phone-only/mobile customers.
coaching_implication: This is a positive, replicable moment — highlight it to the rep as the correct model for handling mobile customers, since other reps on the floor burn 8-15 minutes on this exact scenario.

quote: Well, my psychiatrist worries about it, but
stewart_read: Customer discloses a mental-health-adjacent vulnerability (psychiatrist) immediately followed later by an unprompted insomnia/sleep-deprivation disclosure at 09:58-10:05; the rep responds to the first with only "Man" (09:22) and to the second with "Gosh. Okay" (10:11) — acknowledgment without any bridge to how the appointment or solar solution accommodates his situation.
coaching_implication: Both disclosures are trust gifts per the schema. Coach the rep to acknowledge specifically and bridge to value or logistics (e.g., confirming the afternoon slot respects his sleep schedule) rather than filler reactions.

quote: we're gonna come we're gonna we're gonna come up with a way of covering my electric my my requirements for electricity 100%.
stewart_read: Customer states a 100% offset goal directly; rep's response is a flat "Okay" (14:07) with no reflection or curiosity-building line about what that would look like on the design.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be intentionally holding back detail since the closer will build and present the actual numbers — deferring specifics is schema-correct scope discipline.
coaching_implication: The scope-discipline read has merit, but a brief acknowledging reflection ("that's exactly the kind of target our specialist will build the design around") costs nothing and keeps the customer's own goal anchored for the appointment.

quote: you're not the first one to reach out to me from ION
stewart_read: Customer reveals prior Ion contacts who promised callbacks and didn't deliver, plus a specific missed-callback promise ("I was told you would call me no later than 01:00 today"). The rep offers a brief apology and does not ask who contacted him before, what was promised, or how many times.
coaching_implication: This is competitive/internal-process intelligence the closer needs. A 10-second probe ("do you remember who you spoke with, or when?") would have surfaced whether this is a lead-routing problem worth flagging internally.

quote: The best I've been able to get out of them so far is providing 65% of what they think I need.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he has other companies actively quoting him and describes a specific technical shortfall (only 65% coverage, 36 feet of usable roof run) they found. Rep acknowledges ("Right") but never asks which companies or requests more detail for competitive context.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be avoiding a technical debate about roof constraints, correctly deferring to the specialist per setter_scope_discipline.
coaching_implication: Scope discipline on the technical roof debate is correct, but naming the competing companies is separate, low-risk, high-value information that should still be captured for the closer.
